official.title: Postdoc Researcher in Subsurface Imaging and Scanning Electron Microscopy
official.description_text:
Explore how electron signals can reveal hidden structures in next-generation semiconductor devices. Join TU Delft and ASML to advance scanning electron microscopy and develop innovative detection concepts that improve the imaging of structures below the surface.
Job description
Semiconductor devices are becoming increasingly small and complex. As a result, critical structures and defects are more difficult to detect using conventional inspection methods. Improving subsurface imaging is essential to advancing semiconductor technology and enabling the next generation of electronic devices.
At TU Delft, in collaboration with ASML, you will investigate how backscattered electrons (BSE) can reveal information about buried structures in semiconductor devices. Your research will focus on understanding which components of the electron signal contain the most useful information and how these can be detected more effectively.
You will explore four interconnected research themes: the physics and information content of backscattered electron signals, the influence of electron beam and sample parameters, the fundamental limits of resolution and detectability, and the development of detector concepts that capture more relevant information.
Combining theoretical modelling, scanning electron microscopy experiments and detector-concept development, you will translate fundamental insights into practical improvements in subsurface imaging. Your work will contribute to better resolution, improved signal-to-noise ratios and faster image acquisition.
You will work in an interdisciplinary research environment, collaborating with experts from TU Delft and ASML. You will also have opportunities to co-supervise PhD and MSc students, contribute to scientific discussions and strengthen your research leadership skills.
This postdoctoral position offers the opportunity to connect fundamental electron microscopy research with industrial challenges and contribute to innovations in semiconductor inspection. You will have room to develop your expertise, take ownership of research activities and build collaborations across academia and industry.
Job requirements
You get a kick out of using applied science to solve complex problems. With your pioneering mindset, you can handle the uncertainties of the unknown.
You also have:
A PhD in Engineering, Science, (Applied) Physics, (Applied) Chemistry or a closely related discipline.
Demonstrable research experience in scanning electron microscopy (SEM), preferably involving nanoscale imaging.
A solid understanding of electron microscopy principles and an interest in the physics of backscattered electron signals.
Experience with experimental research, modelling or developing and improving technical measurement systems.
Enjoyment in tinkering with machines and enthusiasm for testing equipment, troubleshooting and implementing technical improvements.
Strong organisational skills and the ability to plan and drive research activities independently.
An interest in developing leadership skills and co-supervising PhD and MSc students.
Excellent English communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively in an international, interdisciplinary environment.
TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
Faculty Applied Sciences
With more than 1,100 employees, including 150 pioneering principal investigators, as well as a population of about 3,600 passionate students, the Faculty of Applied Sciences is an inspiring scientific ecosystem. Focusing on key enabling technologies, such as quantum- and nanotechnology, photonics, biotechnology, synthetic biology and materials for energy storage and conversion, our faculty aims to provide solutions to important problems of the 21st century. To that end, we educate innovative students in broad Bachelor's and specialist Master's programmes with a strong research component. Our scientists conduct ground-breaking fundamental and applied research in the fields of Life and Health Science & Technology, Nanoscience, Chemical Engineering, Radiation Science & Technology, and Engineering Physics. We are also training the next generation of high school teachers.

Attention for working healthy and energetically with the vitality program.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position in scanning electron microscopy and subsurface imaging for semiconductor inspection at TU Delft in collaboration with ASML. Focus is on physics of backscattered electron signals, detector development, and experimental characterization of nanoscale structures.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is fundamentally rooted in electron microscopy physics, materials characterization, and semiconductor instrumentation. The researcher's domain is human-centred immersive systems, spatial cognition, and collaborative learning. No thematic overlap in content, methodology, or research questions.

methodological_fit.rationale: Weak methodological connection: position requires experimental design and technical troubleshooting, which the researcher has experience with. However, the researcher's experimental work focuses on user studies and cognitive outcomes, not instrumentation physics or signal detection. Supervision of students is mentioned but represents only a minor component of this role.

growth_value.rationale: Minimal relevance to target identity or long-term capability development. The researcher would gain expertise in electron microscopy, detector physics, and semiconductor imaging—none of which align with human-centred XR, spatial learning, or collaborative systems research.

strategic_value.rationale: TU Delft is a strong institution in the researcher's priority-2 list (European fit), which provides some institutional credibility. ASML collaboration offers industry exposure. However, the research direction is orthogonal to stated goals and does not advance the researcher toward a human-centred immersive systems trajectory. The postdoc timeframe (1 year) is short and would not establish a research foothold in target domains.

eligibility_flags: Researcher holds MSc by Research (in progress, thesis stage); position requires completed PhD. Not currently eligible unless thesis is completed and degree conferred before employment start.
risks: PhD eligibility gap: researcher is at thesis stage and would need to complete degree before or by employment decision date.
Complete domain mismatch: accepting this role would signal a pivot away from human-centred XR research and delay progress toward stated target identity.
Short contract (1 year) leaves minimal time to build expertise in unfamiliar instrumentation domain.
Limited collaborative value: research group has no overlap with priority institutions (Aalto, TU Delft focused HCI groups) or human-centred immersive systems communities.
